exercises.name: Da Ga
exercises.details: Alternate the tip and the back of your tongue with a voiced "D" and "G". Keep your voice going so the notes stay connected.

exercises.name: Ya Ya
exercises.details: Move only your tongue for each "Y" and keep your jaw still. Rest a finger on your chin if it wants to join in.

exercises.name: Doo Bee Doo
exercises.details: Sing it like a relaxed jazz scat. Keep the consonants light and let the notes swing into each other.

exercises.name: Kee Kay Kah Koh Koo
exercises.details: Keep a crisp "K" on every note and change only the vowel. The back of your tongue should spring away quickly.

exercises.name: Rrr Rah
exercises.details: Roll your tongue on the way up, then let the trill open into "Rah". Keep the air as steady as it was during the trill.

exercises.name: Lee Loo
exercises.details: Flick a light "L" on each note and switch between a narrow "Ee" and a round "Oo". Keep the line smooth and connected.

exercises.name: Bee Boo Bah
exercises.details: Let your lips bounce off each "B" and keep the three vowels clearly different. The air should keep flowing between them.

exercises.name: Zah Sah
exercises.details: Switch between a buzzing "Z" and a hissing "S". The vowel should come in on pitch right after each consonant.

exercises.name: Mah Nah Lah
exercises.details: Move from the lips to the tip of the tongue and back again. Keep each consonant quick and the "Ah" open behind it.

exercises.name: Dit Dat
exercises.details: Make every note short and crisp, with the "T" cutting it off cleanly. Keep a small silence between the notes.

exercises.name: Ki Ka Ku
exercises.details: Spring off the back of your tongue on every "K". Keep the notes bright and bouncy, and don't let the leaps slow you down.

exercises.name: Yah Yeh Yee Yoh Yoo
exercises.details: Glide through the vowels with a light "Y" and keep your jaw loose. Only your tongue and lips should change shape.

exercises.name: Nah Dah
exercises.details: Switch between a nasal "N" and a clean "D" while your tongue stays behind your teeth. Only the soft palate should move.

exercises.name: Shoo Bee Doo Wah
exercises.details: A four-syllable scat line. Keep it relaxed and rhythmic, and give each consonant a clear but gentle start.

exercises.name: Staccato Hee
exercises.details: Give each "Hee" a tiny bounce from your belly, like a giggle. Stay light and let the notes spring off one another.

exercises.name: Gah Bah
exercises.details: Jump between the back of your tongue and your lips on every note. Keep the rhythm even as the consonants alternate.

exercises.name: Descending Thirds
exercises.details: Start the top note light and keep the skips even on the way down. Don't let the low notes get heavier.
